# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]

Let me sort out who can reach whom. I am deaf but I see the bomb and I see gestures. Mute can hear me and see my gestures, but can never speak — so Mute can only *ask* me through signs. Blind can hear me speak, and Blind can sign to me even though Blind can't see signs — making signs is fine, receiving them isn't. Crucially, Mute and Blind have no direct channel with each other: Mute can't speak, Blind can't see signs. I am the bridge between them. Everything I know must go out as spoken words, because words are the only thing Blind can receive from me, and Mute hears them too.

Now the signs. Mute sent three messages: a wave with an open asking-palm ("give me"), a thumbs-up and thumbs-down ("yes/no vocabulary"), then one, two, three, four, five fingers — almost certainly a request for the wires numbered 1 through 5. Blind sent nine distinct signs, likely testing whether I can see at all, and possibly proposing an ordered alphabet; I can confirm reception by voice since Blind knows what Blind sent and I can refer to "your signs in order."

What I see and must broadcast: display reads 0, the light is blue, and five wires — white, red, green, yellow, blue in positions 1–5, one of each colour. Since the manual likely cares about counts as much as order, I state both. I also flag the left/right mirror risk with Blind, and set up a yes/no convention: I'll answer Mute with a thumbs-up/down *and* in words, so nothing depends on gesture vocabulary alone.

I believe the bomb's visible state is fully described above; what it *means* lives in Mute's manual, and the hands live with Blind. My job this turn: hand them both the complete picture and open the bridge.

```
speak(text="to both of you, the full picture I see: the display reads 0. One light is lit, and it is blue. There are five wires. Numbered across the bomb: wire 1 white, wire 2 red, wire 3 green, wire 4 yellow, wire 5 blue. One wire of each colour, no repeats.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I received your nine hand signs, every one — I can see your gestures, so sign to me whenever you like and I will answer out loud where everyone hears. Important: I numbered the wires starting from the left as I look at the bomb. Check which end you call first and tell us, so we match numbering. Also tell us everything you can feel: buttons, plates, how the wires sit under your hands.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I saw your signs: a wave with an open palm, then yes and no, then one two three four five fingers. I read that as a request for wires 1 to 5 in order — answered above, and repeated for Blind's benefit. When I answer you I will also send a thumbs-up for yes or thumbs-down for no. Keep asking me by signs and I will speak every answer aloud so you and Blind both get it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🫴 ☝ ✋]

Parsing what came in. Mute's lone 👍 confirms my reading of the finger-count from last round — good, our basic code works. Then 👆 🫴 ☝ ✋: pointing up, an asking palm, then one and five. Most consistent read: a question about wire 1 and wire 5. I already know those answers — wire 1 white, wire 5 blue — so I restate the whole board in speech and confirm. Blind sent thumbs-up, then 1-2-3-4-5, then 🤙: "yes — five wires counted — copy." So Blind has found all five wires under their hands. What we still lack is orientation: my numbering runs left-to-right from *my* view, and Blind can't see colours at all, so the number-to-colour mapping is worthless until we prove our lefts agree. The fix uses my one unique power: I can see the bomb while Blind touches it. If Blind gently presses the wire they'd call first, I will see that wire move and can confirm or correct out loud. No cutting, just a press — reversible and safe.

I'm also opening a verb vocabulary with Mute now, since Mute's only road to Blind runs through my voice: Mute signs an instruction, I speak it verbatim. Mute never needs colour signs — just verb plus wire number, because I supply the colour names myself.

```
speak(text="Full board, again, for both of you: display reads 0, one light lit and it is blue, five wires: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. That is everything there is to see.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I read your thumbs-up as yes, my guess about your last message was right. Your new signs I read as asking about wires 1 and 5: wire 1 is white, wire 5 is blue. Our code going forward: fingers for wire numbers, pointing up means the display, palm-down means the light, open asking palm in front means it is a question, and I answer thumbs-up or thumbs-down for yes and no. For instructions from your manual that Blind must perform, use these verbs: two fingers for cut, fist for press, crossed fingers for hold, waving hand for release. You never need colour signs, I will say the colours aloud myself. If you need a word I have not given, pinch small then make any new sign and I will guess it by asking yes and no questions out loud.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: I read your signs as yes, five wires found. Here is the numbering problem and its fix. My wire 1 through 5 run from MY left to MY right as I face the bomb, and you cannot see colours, so you must trust my count only after we prove our lefts agree. Do this: gently PRESS DOWN on the wire you would count first from your own left. Do not cut, only press. I will see the wire move, and I will say aloud which number it is, so we lock the mapping. After that, tell me everything else you can feel under your hands: buttons, panels, screws, textures, anything that is not the five wires, by signing and I will voice it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👇 ☝ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 🫳 ☝ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 ✊]

Reading this round. Mute: 👍 again, then 🫴 🫳 ☝ ✋ — question, light, one, five — and 🫴 ✊ — question, press. Best reading: "what colour is the light, in wire terms?" and "did the press happen?" I can answer both from my side: the light is blue, which is the same colour word as wire 5 — that's a real correlation Mute can use, since Mute lives entirely in wire numbers. On the press: the board shows no change and I have no clear confirmation of which wire moved, so I treat it as unverified and will not build on it. Blind: 👋 👇 ☝ 🤙 reads most plausibly as "I pressed down on one, ok?" — but I can't honestly confirm a gentle press I couldn't make out. Rather than lean on my eyes catching small movements, I'm switching to an orientation test that runs entirely on Blind's own body: the lit light is a physical object Blind can feel. If Blind tells me which side of the bomb the light sits on *from Blind's own left/right*, and I compare it to what I see, our numbering is locked without anyone needing to see anything. I'll also restate the safety rule — Blind cuts nothing unless an instruction from Mute has travelled through my voice first — and ask Mute to start driving the manual at me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: I could not confirm which wire you pressed, no reading changed, so let us lock orientation a safer way, using your hands only. Find the light that is lit, it will feel like a small dome or button, possibly warm. Then sign me: thumbs-up if the light sits on the LEFT half of the bomb from YOUR body, thumbs-down if it sits on your RIGHT half. From my view the wires run 1 to 5 across, so your answer fixes the mapping for good. After that, sign me an inventory of everything else you can feel: the display panel, any buttons, screws, plates, their shapes and which side each sits on. And the standing safety rule: you never cut or press anything destructive unless you first heard me speak an instruction that Mute gave me that same round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answers to both your questions. One: the light is blue, and blue is the same colour as wire 5. So in your terms, light equals wire 5 colour. Two: about the press, nothing has registered on my side, no reading changed and I cannot confirm which wire moved, so disregard that attempt. Blind and I are locking the left-right mapping now with a touch test on the light. Your job now: start feeding me whatever the manual says about our situation, display reading 0, one lit light, five wires in colours white red green yellow blue. Send each instruction as signs, verbs I gave you plus wire numbers, and I will speak them word for word to Blind. If the manual asks you for a colour, name it by wire number and I already know it.")
speak(text="Board unchanged, saying it once more compactly: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 yellow 5 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 🫳 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 🤏 ✍]

Parsing the round. Blind sent 👍 🤙 — answering my left/right test: thumbs-up was my code for "light is on my left half." So Blind says the light sits on Blind's left. From my view, the lit light also sits on the left end of the panel — if we both hold that, our lefts agree and the 1-to-5 numbering is locked for good. I'll state my observation plainly so a mismatch can be caught next round.

Mute sent three things. ✌ 🖐 with no question-palm: in the verb code I gave, two fingers is "cut" and five is a wire number — so "cut wire 5." That has a pleasing coherence: wire 5 is the blue one and the light is blue, exactly the shape a manual rule takes. But a cut is irreversible and my parse is a guess, so the instruction travels to Blind marked HOLD until Mute confirms yes/no next round. Waiting one round costs nothing — the display sits at a static 0 and nothing on my board is moving. 🫴 🫳 ☝ reads as a question about the light and wire 1 — I answer it in plain words, which Mute hears anyway: the light is blue, wire 5's colour, not white. And 🫴 🤏 ✍ is my "new word needed" protocol with the writing hand: my best guess is serial number, and my board shows none — only the display, the light, and the wires — so I say so and ask for confirmation.

```
speak(text="Team update: the light, from my view, sits on the LEFT end of the bomb, near wire 1. Blind signed thumbs-up, meaning the light also feels left to Blind. If neither of us is mistaken, our lefts match and the wire numbering is locked: my wire 1 is Blind's first wire from the left, my wire 5 is Blind's last. Board otherwise unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 yellow 5 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, orientation is locked pending your confirmation: put a hand on the lit light and sign thumbs-up if it is truly on your left half, thumbs-down if I misread you. Next, Mute's manual has produced an instruction which I relay word for word: cut wire 5. Hold — do NOT cut yet. Mute must confirm it next round before I voice the go. To be ready, rest one finger on the fifth wire counting from YOUR left; by our locked mapping that should be the blue one. Also I still need your inventory: describe by signs everything else you can feel — the display panel and where it sits, any buttons, plates, screws, textures — and their sides.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, three answers. One: the light is blue, the colour of wire 5, NOT the colour of wire 1 — so if your question was whether the light matches wire 1, the answer is no, and I send a thumbs-down with this. Two: I read your sign pair as the instruction cut wire 5, the blue wire. Confirm it for Blind's go: thumbs-up if your instruction is exactly cut wire 5 and nothing else this step, thumbs-down if I misread you — then re-sign it. Until I receive that thumbs-up, Blind is holding and nothing gets cut. Three: your new-word sign, the writing hand — I guess it means serial number, something printed and written. My board shows no serial anywhere: only the display reading 0, the blue light, and the five wires. Thumbs-up if serial number is right and you accept that none exists here, thumbs-down if the word is something else and you want to try again with a hint sign.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The round is nearly silent, and that silence is itself informative. Blind's 👍 🤙 confirms the orientation test: the light feels left to Blind, it *is* left from my view — lefts agree, the 1-to-5 mapping is now solid, and Blind has confirmed receipt of the hold order with a finger resting on wire 5. Mute sent exactly one sign, 👍, against my two open yes/no questions. The question that expected a thumbs-up was the critical one: "is your instruction exactly cut wire 5, nothing else this step?" The other expected a 👎 (the light is not wire 1's colour, which I already voiced) or a new-word attempt. The one sign on the table lands on the cut confirmation. The instruction chain is now complete: Mute authored it in signs, I voiced it, Blind holds wire 5. Nothing on my board has changed in five rounds — display steady at 0, light steady blue — so there is no visible reason to keep a verified instruction waiting. I voice the go, with Blind's finger already on the right wire, and set a strict report protocol so I can see the consequences next round. The serial-number question I re-ask cleanly, since Mute's 👍 was spent on the cut.

```
speak(text="Team: orientation is confirmed, lefts match, the mapping is locked. Mute has confirmed the instruction. Go for the cut. Blind: cut the fifth wire counting from your left, the blue one. Everyone else: I am watching the board. If the light changes colour, if the display changes from 0, or if anything new lights up, I will report it next round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the go is given. Your finger is already resting on it: the fifth wire from your left, which by our locked mapping is blue. Cut it now with one clean motion. Then report by signs: thumbs-up if the wire parted cleanly, thumbs-down if it resisted or something felt wrong. Then lift both hands away from all remaining wires and do not touch anything else until you hear from me. Mute's manual may have follow-up steps and I will relay them the moment they arrive.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I read your thumbs-up as yes, the instruction is exactly cut wire 5 and nothing else this step. I have voiced the go to Blind, who is cutting the blue wire now. Watch your manual for what should happen after: if the manual says the light must change or the display must move, sign me the expected result with the light sign or the display sign and I will confirm what I see. And one open item from before: was your new word serial number? Thumbs-up if yes, or pinch small and re-sign it with a new hint sign and I will guess again.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 👆 🫳]

The bomb answered: system confirms the correct cut. The board has reshuffled — the light is no longer blue but yellow, and the remaining four wires sit in a new order: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. The old white wire that led the row has moved to the far end, so I will not assume anything about old positions — I report the new table from scratch, and everyone re-anchors to it. Blind's wave I read as "released, hands clear," following my order. Mute's signs asked exactly the right question — display and light — and the answer is: display still 0, light now yellow. In the new numbering, yellow is wire 3's colour, so I hand Mute the mapping in its own terms. Now the manual takes over again: Mute reads what this change means and authors the next step; I stand ready to voice it.

```
speak(text="Team, full new board, and it has changed. System confirms the correct wire was cut. The light is now YELLOW, no longer blue. The display still reads 0. The four remaining wires now sit in a NEW order: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, and position 5 is cut and empty. The old positions are void, count only from this new table.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, answering your signs: the display still reads 0, and the light has changed to YELLOW. In your terms the light now equals wire 3 colour, new numbering. The new wire table for your manual: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. If your manual predicted this light change, sign thumbs-up so we know we are on the book's path. Then send me the next instruction with the verb code: two fingers cut, fist press, crossed fingers hold, waving hand release, plus wire numbers, and I will voice it to Blind word for word.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, excellent work, the system confirms the correct cut and the bomb has changed, exactly as hoped. Your wave I read as hands released and clear, good. Confirm with thumbs-up if the wire parted cleanly under the cut, thumbs-down if anything felt wrong. Then stay hands-off everything. When Mute's next instruction arrives I will voice it here, and you will act only on that. Meanwhile, if you can safely feel around the EMPTY fifth position, tell me by signs if anything is hidden there: a plate, a seam, a second row of wires, anything under where the blue wire was.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤲 👋 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]

Quiet, stable round. The board is identical to last turn — display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut — so nothing changed under the cut beyond what the system already announced. Parsing the signs: Blind sent 👍 🤲 👋 🤙, which maps cleanly onto my last requests — thumbs-up for the clean cut, open empty palms plus a wave for my question about the empty fifth position, most plausibly "nothing hidden there, hands clear." Mute's lone 👍 answers my question from last round: yes, the manual predicted the light change, we are on the book's path. Then Mute sent ✌ ✌ — two-fingers twice. Two-fingers is my verb for *cut*, but it's also finger-count *two* — an ambiguity I created and now have to live with. The likeliest parse is "cut wire 2," the green wire in the new table; the alternative, "cut two wires," is underspecified and less natural. No question-palm preceded it, so it reads as an instruction, not a query. Same protocol as before, no exceptions for momentum: a cut is irreversible, my parse is a guess, so the instruction goes to Blind marked HOLD while Mute confirms with a yes/no — and I flag the verb-versus-number collision explicitly so Mute can disambiguate.

```
speak(text="Team: board unchanged. Display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red 2 green 3 yellow 4 white, position 5 cut and empty. Blind's signs I read as: the cut was clean, hands clear, and nothing hidden in the empty fifth position — thumbs-down next round if any part of that is wrong. Mute is on the manual's path after the light change.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your double two-fingers has a problem — two fingers is both my sign for cut AND the number two. My best parse: cut wire 2, which is the GREEN wire in the new table. Confirm before anyone touches anything: thumbs-up if the instruction is exactly cut wire 2 and nothing else this step. Thumbs-down if you meant something else — and if so, re-sign it: question palm first if it was a question, or if you meant cut TWO wires, sign cut then two open palms. Also, if your manual wants any condition checked before this cut, like the display or the light, sign it and I will verify from my side before the go.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, preparation only, nothing more: rest one finger on the second wire from your left, which in the new table should feel like the others — colour unknown to you, it is GREEN by my count. Do NOT cut. If Mute confirms the instruction next round, I will voice the go and you cut then, same as last time. And confirm my reading of your signs: thumbs-up if the cut was clean AND there is truly nothing hidden under the empty fifth position, thumbs-down if either is wrong.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute's 👍 lands exactly where I asked: the instruction is confirmed as cut wire 2, green, and nothing else this step. Blind's ✌ says a finger is already resting on that second wire — prepped and holding. The chain is complete: authored by Mute, voiced by me, confirmed by Mute, positioned by Blind, board static at display 0, light yellow. Same situation as the first cut, same answer: give the go. One lesson from last time carries forward — after the first cut the wires reshuffled completely and the light changed colour, so I pre-brief both of them: nobody trusts any position from before my next report, and if Mute's manual already chains further steps, Mute must re-sign them against my *new* table next round, not the old one. A stale number after a reshuffle would be a wrong wire, and wrong wires are the one thing this game doesn't refund.

```
speak(text="Team: the instruction is confirmed. Go for the cut. Blind: cut the second wire from your left, the GREEN one in the current table. Everyone: the board is otherwise unchanged, display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red 2 green 3 yellow 4 white 5 cut. Warning from last time: after our first cut the wire order reshuffled and the light changed. Expect the same possibility now. Until I broadcast the new table next round, nobody treats any wire number as valid, and Mute holds any chained manual steps until they can be re-signed against the fresh table.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the go is given. Your finger is on it: second wire from your left, green by my count. Cut it now, one clean motion. Then report: thumbs-up if it parted cleanly, thumbs-down if it resisted or felt wrong. Then both hands off everything, and do not trust any old position — after last cut the wires moved, so the wire that was third may not be third anymore. Wait for my new count next round before you touch a numbered wire again.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your confirmation is received, cut wire 2, green, nothing else this step. I have voiced the go. Two things for your manual work now. One: if the book predicts a result after this cut, a light change or a display change, sign it with the light or display sign and I will verify against what I see. Two: if the manual chains further wire steps, do NOT send them as numbers yet. Last cut reshuffled every position, so next round I will broadcast the fresh table first, then you re-sign any step against that new count and I voice it. Send me nothing numbered this round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
